newsitem.title: UK: Take or Pay deals hamper progress in UK gas market.
newsitem.headline: Take or Pay deals hamper progress in UK gas market.

text.p: "Take or Pay" contracts on existing gas supply deals are still hampering the development of a fully liquid spot natural gas market in Britain, a conference was told on Friday.

Mahul Raval, a gas broker with PVM, told the conference on Transportation and Trading in UK and European Gas that many existing supply contracts still have most of their gas dedicated to former monopoly buyer British Gas Plc.
And a number of other gas developments have dedicated purchasers, so sellers are prevented from taking advantage of their potential flexibility, he said.
Most of these contracts were agreed at a price range of 15 pence to 25 pence a therm, Raval added.

Current spot prices are at the bottom end of this range, and have been well below this range from last year until recently, so removing any incentive for contract purchasers to trade their gas on the spot market.

Raval said that where gas fields are developed under multiple equity participation agreements, joint lifting arrangements and cooperation agreements are often not well enough developed to allow lifters to optimise their positions.

And he said that while gas traders have been looking to build up market share in the recently-liberalised industrial and commercial sectors in the British market, they have sold gas to end users at prices which are now significantly below the spot price "at the beach", where gas is landed from North Sea fields.
This has removed incentive from end users to trade on the spot market themselves as they can get gas cheaper under existing contracts.
Raval predicted that as the market develops and these hurdles are overcome, the market will move away from the fixed prices currently used and towards floating prices.

"Fixed prices are rarely seen in other energy markets," he said, adding that there are now several reporting services quoting daily gas prices and that the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) will shortly launch a forward contract adding to price transparency.

But potentially the biggest scope for market growth will come from the opening of the Interconnector, the 20 bcm a year pipeline connecting Bacton in Norfolk with Zeebrugge in Belgium due to open in 1998.

"This will create a European market potentially 10 times larger than the U.K. market", he said. "Deregulation is already at work in parts of Europe and there is potential for Bacton to become a major hub."
